title: Concerns and Values in Human-Robot Interactions: A Focus on Social Robotics

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptually evaluated as a core ethical concern in human-robot interaction (HRI) through a scoping literature review and expert focus groups, ultimately being integrated as an evaluation metric in the proposed HRI Value Compass design tool.

Conceptually evaluated via expert focus groups, which highlighted the risk of data-driven robots reinforcing gender stereotypes or exacerbating disparities in domestic tasks based on biased training data.

Conceptually evaluated via expert focus groups, noting the risk that robots might struggle to accurately identify emotional states or interact equitably with children from varying socioeconomic backgrounds.
Conceptually evaluated via expert focus groups, identifying the ethical risk of robotic models failing to accurately assess or appropriately interact with users of varying cognitive abilities.
